bibl.title: dna2vec: Consistent Vector Representations of Variable-Length k-mers

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: In this paper, we propose a novel method to train distributed representations of variable-length k-mers.

span.label: distributed vector representations of DNA k-mers
span.quote: The usage of k-mer representation has been a popular approach in analyzing long sequence of DNA fragments.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: The two-layer neural network training method described in Section 2.3 was implemented using gensim framework (Řehůřek and Sojka, 2010).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: training word2vec (CBOW/skip-gram) on overlapping variable-length DNA k-mers
span.quote: we propose a novel method to train distributed representations of variable-length k-mers

span.label: The standard encoding asserts that every pair of sequences is equally unlike every other, which is false of the sequences themselves.
span.quote: Worse yet, the distance between any arbitrary pair of one-hot vectors is equidistant, even though ATGGC should be closer to ATGGG than CACGA

span.label: Every similarity result in the paper is measured against one stipulated alignment scoring, including a gap penalty of zero.
span.quote: All of the Needleman-Wunsch similarity score in this paper were computed using Biopython’s align.globalxx function, which used a match score of 1, mismatch of 0 and gap penalty of 0

span.label: The method's justification is a hypothesis about words, carried over to nucleotides, and the paper marks the inspiration as loose.
span.quote: This reconstruction of context of words is loosely inspired by the linguistic concept of distributional hypothesis, which states that words that appear in the same context have similar meaning

span.label: the word2vec word-embedding model, applied to DNA k-mers
span.quote: Our method is based on the popular word embedding model word2vec, which is trained on a shallow two-layer neural network

span.label: context - AS PHYSICAL ADJACENCY ALONG THE SEQUENCE: the set of k-mers next to the target within a fragment, which is what the word means here, not linguistic co-occurrence
span.quote: Our dna2vec algorithm is trained by predicting the “context” surrounding a given targeted k-mer. The “context” is the set of adjacent k-mers surrounding the targeted k-mer

span.label: the distributional hypothesis - AS THE TRANSFERRED WARRANT: a 1954 claim about words in the same context having similar meaning, doing the justificatory work for a model of nucleotides
span.quote: the linguistic concept of distributional hypothesis, which states that words that appear in the same context have similar meaning

span.label: k-mer length - AS A RANDOM VARIABLE: the window size is drawn from a discrete uniform distribution for each position, so the same sequence yields different k-mers on different runs
span.quote: we sample k from the discrete uniform distribution Uniform(klow, khigh) to determine the size of each window

span.label: builds-on → word2vec (from NLP/linguistics)
span.quote: Our method is based on the popular word embedding model word2vec

span.label: builds-on → word2vec (Mikolov et al., 2013a)
span.quote: Our method is based on the popular word embedding model word2vec, which is trained on a shallow two-layer neural network.

span.label: extends → BioVec (Asgari and Mofrad, 2015) and seq2vec (Kimothi et al., 2016)
span.quote: Although both techniques used a two-layer neural network to train their embedding, our technique is a generalization for variable-length k.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · k-mer —operationalised-as→ one-hot vector
span.quote: its straightforward vector encoding as a one-hot vector (i.e. bit vector that consists of all zeros except for a single dimension) is vulnerable to curse of dimensionality

span.label: dna2vec —operationalised-as→ word2vec
span.quote: The training method of our shallow two-layer neural network for dna2vec is based on word2vec

span.label: k-mer —operationalised-as→ one-hot vector
span.quote: Unfortunately, the straightforward vector encoding of k-mer as a one-hot vector is vulnerable to the curse of dimensionality.

span.label: 100 — dimensionality of the continuous dna2vec vector space
span.quote: into a continuous vector space of 100 dimensions

span.label: two-layer — depth of the shallow neural network (as in word2vec)
span.quote: trained on a shallow two-layer neural network

span.label: dna2vec adapts word2vec to learn distributed vector representations of variable-length DNA k-mers, avoiding the curse of dimensionality and equidistance of one-hot encodings.
span.quote: we propose a novel method to train distributed representations of variable-length k-mers. Our method is based on the popular word embedding model word2vec

span.label: Summing dna2vec vectors approximates nucleotide concatenation, and cosine similarity of the vectors correlates with Needleman-Wunsch alignment similarity.
span.quote: the summing of dna2vec vectors is akin to nucleotides concatenation. We also demonstrate that there is correlation between Needleman-Wunsch similarity score and cosine similarity of dna2vec vectors.

span.label: DNA k-mer (input token)
span.quote: convert long DNA fragments into overlapping variable-length k-mers

span.label: cosine similarity of dna2vec vectors
span.quote: correlation between Needleman-Wunsch similarity score and cosine similarity of dna2vec vectors

span.label: k-mer
span.quote: One of the ubiquitous representation of long DNA sequence is dividing it into shorter k-mer components

span.label: one-hot vector
span.quote: a one-hot vector (i.e. bit vector that consists of all zeros except for a single dimension)
